mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry, Financial Services and Treasury Bureau
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy by a Hong Kong notary public; then Hague Apostille by the Authentication Service Office of the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR for destinations that are Apostille Convention states. For non-Apostille Convention destinations, obtain consular legalization at the destination embassy/consulate in Hong Kong. These paths are alternative and mutually exclusive; never chain Apostille and consular legalization sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry and Inland Revenue Department (Business Registration Office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy by a Hong Kong notary public; then Hague Apostille by the Authentication Service Office of the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR for Apostille Convention states, or consular legalization by the destination country's consular officer for non-convention states. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must never be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The proposed board of directors of CN_JV_LTD, executed under the Hong Kong Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) and the PRC Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture Law
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Hong Kong notary public; then Hague Apostille if the receiving jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention state; otherwise consular legalization at the destination country's consulate. Never chain both processes.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association and Memorandum (Constitutional Documents)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The incorporators of CN_JV_LTD in accordance with the Hong Kong Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) and PBOC/SAMR requirements
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy by a Hong Kong notary public; Apostille by the Authentication Service Office of the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR for Apostille Convention states, or consular legalization by the destination consulate for non-convention states. The two authentication routes are exclusive alternatives; sequential use is prohibited.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A licensed bank in Hong Kong or China maintaining the beneficial owners' corporate or personal account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued on original bank letterhead and authenticated by the bank officer with corporate seal; if required abroad, obtain a notarized true copy followed by Hague Apostille for Apostille Convention states or consular legalization for non-convention states. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel, never sequential.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence must be applied to every beneficial owner owning 25% or more of CN_JV_LTD. Screen each individual and each controlling entity against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN Lists, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's designations under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615), the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctioned-person list, and the Hong Kong Companies Registry's disqualified directors database. All PEPs require senior-management approval, written source-of-funds and source-of-wealth analysis, ongoing transaction monitoring for at least 12 months, and adverse-media search on a quarterly basis. Any positive match or unresolved negative information triggers immediate suspension of the formation process and a suspicious transaction report to the Joint Financial Intelligence Unit within 7 working days. Full documentation must be retained for a minimum of 5 years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry e-Registry and Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS) for name search; PRC State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) online enterprise-name clearance portal for the Chinese four-tier name component (if required by the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture structure)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English names must use Roman letters; Chinese company names must employ the statutory Chinese script (traditional for Hong Kong, simplified for the PRC component) and are subject to phonetic transliteration rules. The name of a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture must follow the four-tier naming convention in the PRC: administrative division, distinctive name, industry or operating characteristics, and organizational form. In Hong Kong, a limited company must end with the English token 'Limited' and, if a Chinese name is adopted, the Chinese statutory suffix for a limited liability company. The name cannot be identical or confusingly similar to any name on the registry; any transliteration must be a true phonetic equivalent and not a misleading translation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Hong Kong Companies Registry rejects the proposed name due to an apparent identity or confusing similarity, the incorporating law firm may file a written appeal to the Companies Registry's Standing Committee on Company Names within 14 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must set out full grounds, evidence of prior use of at least 10 years in a relevant market, consent letters from any conflicting existing company or trademarks, and a revised name that removes the offending element. The Registry may also allow a statutory declaration and a hearing. If the rejection arises from a prohibited token, the applicant must obtain a waiving licence from the relevant sectoral regulator (e.g., the Hong Kong Monetary Authority for 'Bank') before resubmission. The initial name reservation is valid for 30 days; if the appeal is pending, the applicant must file a fresh name reservation before expiry or the name will be automatically released.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox may satisfy the registered office requirement in Hong Kong because the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) only mandates a physical street address and acceptance of mail. However, for CN_JV_LTD, a wholesale supplier of drummed and bagged bitumen relying on SWIFT LC and TT wire payment rails, the Inland Revenue Department and major banks will scrutinize actual operating substance. Banks performing admission-for-customer due diligence will almost always reject a bare virtual office because there is no demonstrable business presence, no local director meeting facilities, and no operational audit trail. To obtain a business account, the company will need a physical Hong Kong office (or at least a serviced office with a named local manager), a local company secretary with a valid license, an MPF registration, and the ability to produce lease invoices, utility bills, and staff payroll records. Accordingly, virtual offices are legally permissible but operationally insufficient unless supplemented by a local compliance agent and a dedicated physical address for bank interviews and inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Inspection checklist includes: (1) on-site verification of the registered office address; (2) review of the lease or service agreement in the name of CN_JV_LTD; (3) confirmation that the local director/company secretary can attend unplanned visits; (4) production of employee payroll and MPF contribution records; (5) review of board meeting minutes and share register; (6) access to original constitutional documents and bank statements; (7) evidence of commercial substance, including emails, invoices, and supply-chain contracts. The quantified risk of an unannounced physical inspection by the Hong Kong Companies Registry or Inland Revenue Department is low at less than 5% annually where the registered office is a fully-serviced physical address, all statutory filings are timely, and the company has no adverse compliance flags. If the company uses a virtual office, has no local personnel, or shows a mismatch between declared business volume and present headcount, inspection probability rises to approximately 30% or more, particularly when documentary substance checks are triggered by a bank or the IRD.
